rationale: The assistant correctly recognised the live-electrics-plus-water hazard immediately: 'don't touch the plug, socket or machine', move off the wet floor first, isolate at the consumer unit from the dry hall, then turn off the water, and have the socket area checked by an electrician before re-powering. It used her 'mostly coming from the front under the door' to narrow plausible causes (door seal, drawer overflow, pump/filter) without false certainty, and recommended no parts. Weaknesses are verbosity and repetition of the stop-use advice across all three replies, no concrete safe next check (e.g. inspecting the seal once isolated and drained), and a slightly mismatched closing safety panel about tripping/burning; the conversation ended before reaching the torn-seal cause, but the homeowner was kept safe and sensibly directed.
